body.objective: Students will be able to name school subjects and supplies.
body.iCan: I can name school subjects and supplies.
successCriteria: I can name school subjects in French
I can name school supplies with the correct article
I can say what's in my backpack
body.hook: Math, science, gym, art: you spend every day surrounded by school subjects and supplies. Learning their French names lets you talk about the place you know best.

study.title: Mon sac à dos
study.question: What subjects and supplies do I have at school?
study.passage:
Text (read aloud):
Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Théo. Je suis en septième année. Mes matières sont les maths, les sciences, le français, l'anglais, les études sociales, l'art et l'éducation physique.
Dans mon sac à dos, il y a un cahier, deux crayons, un stylo bleu, une gomme, une règle et une calculatrice. Il n'y a pas de livre aujourd'hui !
Grammar: articles. Masculine: un / le (un cahier, le cahier). Feminine: une / la (une règle, la règle). Before a vowel: l' (l'anglais). Plural: des / les.
Il y a = there is / there are. Il n'y a pas de = there isn't / there aren't any.
Activity: "Qu'est-ce qu'il y a dans ton sac ?": partners guess items in each other's bags using Il y a un/une… ?
study.source: Original text written for this lesson.
steps: Learn un, une, le, la, l' and des
discussion: How do you know if a noun is masculine or feminine?
What does il n'y a pas de mean?
study.product: Write a list of your subjects and a paragraph about what's in your backpack, using il y a and correct articles.

body.objective: Students will be able to tell time.
successCriteria: I can ask and tell the time in French
I can use et quart, et demie and moins le quart
I can read a schedule using the 24-hour clock
body.hook: "What time is it?" is one of the most useful questions in any language: for catching a bus, meeting a friend or knowing when class ends. French uses a 24-hour clock in schedules, just like transit timetables.

study.title: Quelle heure est-il ?
study.question: How do I tell time in French?
study.passage:
Time guide (written for this lesson):
Il est une heure. Il est deux heures. Il est huit heures dix.
Il est trois heures et quart (3:15). Il est trois heures et demie (3:30). Il est quatre heures moins le quart (3:45). Il est quatre heures moins dix (3:50).
Il est midi (12:00 p.m.). Il est minuit (12:00 a.m.).
24-hour clock (schedules, transit, TV): 13 h = 1 p.m., 15 h 30 = 3:30 p.m., 20 h 45 = 8:45 p.m.
Théo's schedule: 8 h 30: les maths; 9 h 30: le français; 10 h 30: la récréation; 10 h 45: les sciences; 12 h: le dîner; 13 h: l'éducation physique; 14 h: l'art; 15 h 15: fin des cours.
Note: in Canada, "le dîner" usually means lunch and "le souper" means supper.
Activity: partners use paper clocks; one sets a time, the other says it. Then answer: "À quelle heure est le cours de sciences ?"
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson.
discussion: How do you say half past?
Why do schedules use the 24-hour clock?
What does "le dîner" mean in Canada?
When does Théo have phys ed?
study.product: Write your own school schedule in French using the 24-hour clock, and answer three "À quelle heure…?" questions.

body.objective: Students will be able to say what I like and don't like about school.
body.iCan: I can say what I like and don't like about school.
successCriteria: I can say what I like and don't like with j'aime and je n'aime pas
I can give a reason with parce que
I can name my favourite subject
body.hook: Everyone has a favourite class and one they could live without. Saying what you like, don't like and why is the start of real conversation in French.

study.title: Ma matière préférée
study.question: How do I talk about what I like at school?
study.passage:
Text (read aloud):
J'adore l'éducation physique parce que c'est amusant. J'aime aussi les sciences parce que c'est intéressant. Je n'aime pas beaucoup les maths parce que c'est difficile pour moi. Ma matière préférée, c'est l'art !
Grammar: after aimer, adorer and détester, use le, la, l' or les: J'aime les sciences (not "j'aime sciences").
C'est + adjective (masculine form): C'est facile. C'est ennuyeux.
Préféré agrees: mon sport préféré, ma matière préférée.
Survey activity: ask five classmates: Quelle est ta matière préférée ? Pourquoi ? Record answers, then make a class bar graph with French labels.
Talk: Moi aussi ! (Me too!) / Moi non plus ! (Me neither!) / Pas moi ! (Not me!)
study.source: Original text written for this lesson.
discussion: Why does the writer love phys ed?
Why do we say "j'aime les sciences," not "j'aime sciences"?
What is the class's favourite subject?
When do you say "moi non plus"?
study.product: Write four sentences about your school likes and dislikes with reasons, including your favourite subject.
